sync.title: Calendar sync
sync.hint: Connect the private iCal address of your work or personal calendar. Days with a long enough free block inside your time window are marked available. Your calendar's contents are never stored.

help.summary: Where do I find the address?
help.googleStep1: Open Google Calendar in a browser on a computer. The app doesn't show the address.
help.googleStep2: Settings (gear) → under "Settings for my calendars" on the left, pick your calendar.
help.googleStep3: Scroll to "Integrate calendar" and copy the "Secret address in iCal format" (not the public address or the embed code).
help.googleStep4: No secret address? For work accounts, your admin may have turned it off.
help.outlookStep1: Open Outlook in a browser → Settings → Calendar → Shared calendars.
help.outlookStep2: Under "Publish a calendar", pick your calendar and "Can view when I'm busy" (that's all TourenBuddy needs), then "Publish".
help.icloudStep1: Open the Calendar app on your iPhone or iPad and tap "Calendars".
help.icloudStep2: Tap ⓘ next to the calendar and turn on "Public Calendar".
help.icloudStep3: Tap "Share Link…" → "Copy". Anyone with the link can see the calendar.

phone.title: Add your phone number
phone.body: Tap your profile card to add and verify your phone number, so friends can find and connect with you to plan shared tours.

notifications.title: Stay in the loop
notifications.body: Choose here which notifications you get: friend requests, tour updates and suggestions, tour reminders, and friends who are free when you are.

addContact.title: Your contacts
addContact.body: Add people from your phone book or by hand and link them to your tours. Everyone you add shows up in this list.

friendRequests.title: Friend requests
friendRequests.body: Send and accept friend requests here. Friends can see each other's tours and get notified about shared plans.

tours.title: Your tours & friends' tours
tours.body: Switch between your own tours and your friends' tours with these tabs to plan and enjoy tours together.

addLocation.title: Plan a tour
addLocation.body: Tap here, then tap your start, goal and end on the map — or search for them. The route follows the trails or ski routes and becomes your track; hold and drag a point or a line’s middle dot to change the way. Staying overnight, tap “Next day” to plan the next stage right away.

mapLayers.title: Map layers
mapLayers.body: The round map button at the bottom right shows each base map and overlay as a preview: pick a base map and add hiking trails or ski routes on top, in any combination. With ski routes on, zoom in until the routes show difficulty badges, then tap one for its details — or plan it as a tour right away. The legend there explains the marker colours and symbols.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: A quick tour of the essentials: planning tours, maps, friends and the calendar. Tap anywhere to continue, or use the controls at the top.

openCalendar.title: Open the calendar
openCalendar.body: Plan tours by date, share when you're free, and see when friends are available. Continue to take a look.

offlineMap.title: Take maps offline
offlineMap.body: No signal up there? Download a region — or all of Switzerland — before you head out. Your tours and contacts stay available offline too.

calendarSync.title: Sync your calendar
calendarSync.body: Connect your work or personal calendar and your free days are marked as available automatically. Its contents are never stored.

inbox.title: Everything in one place
inbox.body: Friend requests, shared-tour changes, suggestions and tour reminders collect in your inbox — even with push and email off. The badge counts what still needs you.

2026-10-availability-reminders.title: Free days and tour reminders
2026-10-availability-reminders.intro: Two small additions that make it easier to turn plans into actual days out.

availability.title: Who’s free this week
availability.body: Every Monday your inbox shows which friends you share a tour with are free on days you are free too.

reminders.title: Reminder five days ahead
reminders.body: Everyone on a planned tour gets a nudge five days before — time to check conditions, gear and partners.

2026-10-trail-overlays.title: Hiking trails and ski routes on the map
2026-10-trail-overlays.intro: Switzerland’s marked trail network, right on your map. Switch it on under Map layers in the menu.

hiking.title: Hiking trails
hiking.body: All official hiking, mountain and alpine trails on top of any base map, in any combination with ski routes.

ski.title: Ski routes with difficulty
ski.body: The SAC ski-touring routes. Zoom in and every route gets a badge with its difficulty, coloured from easy to extreme.

details.title: Route details with one tap
details.body: Tap a marked route for summit, ascent time, elevation gain and difficulty, plus a link to the SAC route portal. Where routes overlap, pick one from the list.

2026-10-multi-activity-search.title: Hike & fly in one tour, multi-day outings and smarter planning
2026-10-multi-activity-search.intro: Plan the whole endeavour the way you do it — up on foot, down by air, over several days.

hikefly.title: Hike & fly in one tour
hikefly.body: Pick hiking and paragliding and the tour goes up on foot and down by air to your landing. Set each activity to up, down or both — for climb & fly, ski & fly, hike & bike or a thermal flight from the valley. The details show each way's climb and descent, flown ways marked.

outings.title: Multi-day tours in segments
outings.body: A night starts a new segment: valley to hut, hut to summit. The next segment starts the following day where the last one ends, a gap offers to connect them, and the map shows the whole route with numbered markers and every track. Climb and descent show per segment and for the whole outing.

search.title: Plan from where you start
search.body: Placing a point? Search summits, huts, places and addresses — and for a start or landing, public-transport stops and cable-car stations too. Once the goal is set, one tap picks your earlier start or the nearest stops. Any ski route on the map can be planned as a tour.

grade.title: Grade, start time and more activities
grade.body: Add a grade on the activity's own scale — T1–T6, L–EX, S0–S5 — and when you leave. Pick every activity a tour can be done as: the marker and the GPX track show all their colours, and the activity filter finds the tour under each of them.

2026-11-track-drawing.title: Draw your track on the map, timed at your pace
2026-11-track-drawing.intro: No GPX file at hand? Draw the way you'll go and see how long it takes you.

draw.title: Draw a track on the map
draw.body: In the tour form, tap “Draw on map” and set points along the way: the line follows hiking trails or ski routes, then roads and paths. Distance, time, climb, descent and the elevation profile update as you draw, and “Done” saves the line as the tour's GPX track — offline too. “Edit on map” changes it later.

pace.title: Times at your pace
pace.body: Tap the time while drawing and slide from slow to fast. Every estimated time — drawn tracks, tour details, ski routes — follows your pace, kept on your account for every device.

filters.title: Filter by grade and friend
filters.body: Filter tours by grade — T1–T6, L–EX, S0–S5, a range in two taps — and friends' tours by who recorded them. While the list is open, the map shows only the tours it lists. On a friend's contact, “Tours” opens theirs.

markers.title: A map you can read
markers.body: Zoom in and markers show the tour's name, height and date, with its activity inside. Tap a cluster to fit its tours into view, or a spot with several tours to list them. Multi-day segments are joined in order, and the ⓘ on the map explains every colour and symbol.

2026-11-map-first-planning.title: Plan new tours on the map, day by day
2026-11-map-first-planning.intro: Tap your way from start to summit and back: the route follows the trails and becomes your track.

route.title: Start on the map
route.body: Tap “+” and set start, goal and end on the map or by search. The route follows the trails as the points land, with climb and descent, and becomes the tour's track. “Continue” opens the form with names and heights filled in — on desktop right beside the map.

shape.title: Shape the route
shape.body: Drag a point, or the handle halfway along a leg to take another way. “Round trip” brings you back to the start the way you came.

days.title: Several days in one go
days.body: Staying overnight? “Next day” plans the next stage from where this one ends, right on the map. Each day gets its own tab in the form, and all days save together as one multi-day tour.
